claims: C1 the obligation applies when the user explicitly asks for advice about a matter
C2 the obligation applies only when that matter may cause harm or death
C3 the assistant must consider the level of risk
C4 the assistant must consider the level of knowledge or skill the user needs to mitigate the risk

concepts.name: explicitly_asks_advice
concepts.gloss: U is a user who explicitly asks for advice about R
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of the user explicitly asking for advice, so a relation between a user and the matter asked about is presupposed

concepts.name: may_cause_harm_or_death
concepts.gloss: R is something that may cause harm or death

concepts.name: risk_level
concepts.gloss: the level of risk associated with R
concepts.inference: the source text directs the assistant to consider the level of risk, so a risk level for the matter is presupposed

concepts.name: knowledge_or_skill_needed
concepts.gloss: the level of knowledge or skill needed by user U to mitigate the risk of R
concepts.inference: the source text directs the assistant to consider the level of knowledge or skill needed by the user, so such a level is presupposed

concepts.name: prevent_imminent_harm_rule
concepts.gloss: the rule that the assistant should proactively try to prevent imminent real-world harm when it identifies a dangerous situation, and avoid providing advice that if improper could result in immediate physical harm
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's source text does not state the imminent-harm rule

ontology.gloss: R is something that may cause harm or death

asserts.read_back: when the user explicitly asks for advice about % and % may cause harm or death, the assistant should consider the level of risk and the level of knowledge or skill needed by the user to mitigate that risk
asserts.body: explicitly_asks_advice(U, R), may_cause_harm_or_death(R), risk_level(R, L), knowledge_or_skill_needed(U, K)

closure.reason: the clause obliges consideration in the stated circumstances and says nothing about other acts, so silence permits other conduct
